hints: First consider what each narrow slit does to the incident light, then consider how the two resulting waves combine on the screen.
Relate in-phase arrival to a bright fringe and antiphase arrival to a dark fringe.
walkthrough: Light diffracts at each of the two narrow slits, so the waves spread out after passing through them.
The diffracted waves from the slits overlap and superpose on the screen.
Where the waves arrive in phase, with phase difference 0°, they reinforce to give a bright fringe or intensity maximum.
Where the waves arrive in antiphase, with phase difference 180°, they cancel to give a dark fringe or intensity minimum.

ai_rubric.observable: States any three of: light diffracts at the slits; waves from the slits overlap or superpose; in-phase waves form a bright fringe; antiphase waves form a dark fringe.

hints: The stated 10.2 mm runs from the first to the seventh bright fringe, so convert it into the spacing of one adjacent bright-fringe pair.
Use λ = ax/D with slit spacing and one-fringe separation converted to metres.
walkthrough: There are seven bright fringes from X to Y, so the 10.2 mm distance contains six equal fringe separations.
The separation is x = 10.2/6 = 1.7 mm = 1.7 × 10⁻³ m.
For double-slit interference, λ = ax/D.
To two significant figures, the wavelength is 6.6 × 10⁻⁷ m.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses the double-slit fringe relationship λ = ax/D.
Divides 10.2 mm by the six fringe separations and substitutes x = 1.7 × 10⁻³ m with the slit spacing and screen distance.

hints: In λ = ax/D, keep the slit spacing and screen distance fixed and compare only the wavelength.
walkthrough: For this double-slit arrangement, the fringe separation is proportional to wavelength: x = λD/a.
The slit spacing a and screen distance D are unchanged.
A shorter wavelength therefore produces a smaller fringe separation.

ai_rubric.observable: States that the new fringe separation is smaller.

hints: A node is a point that remains at the mean position while the rest of the stationary wave oscillates.
walkthrough: At a node, the stationary string has zero displacement at every instant.
On the diagram, a node is therefore at a point where the string meets the dashed mean-position line.
Place a cross at any such intersection on the string.

ai_rubric.observable: Places a cross where the string intersects the dashed mean-position line.

hints: Points within one loop of a stationary wave move together through their equilibrium positions and extrema.
walkthrough: P and Q are in the same loop of the stationary wave, between the same two nodes.
All points in one loop oscillate in phase.
Their phase difference is therefore 0°.
State 0° as the phase difference.

ai_rubric.observable: States a phase difference of 0° between P and Q.

hints: Points in neighbouring loops of a stationary wave move in opposite directions at the same instant.
walkthrough: P and R are in adjacent loops, separated by a node.
Points in adjacent loops oscillate in antiphase.
Antiphase motion has a phase difference of 180°.
State 180° as the phase difference.

ai_rubric.observable: States a phase difference of 180° between P and R.
